name: The Machinist
description: Hello there! I'm Cody Manders and i'm junior Engineer aboard this vessel. Yes, i know, I'm probably the outlier here with all those doctors taking part in your mission, but Command said that there isn't much hope for developing sophisticated tech on this planet anyway, and Chief Engineer Lichtinger is busy keeping the ship from falling apart, so i will be your advisor on all things technical. I hope we can find some workarounds to this predicament.

quests.name: Greenhouses
quests.description: Greenhouses are a piece of iron age tech that can help you automate and accelerate the growing of crops, even in harsh climates. to make one, craft a climate station, greenhouse walls and rooves, aswell as a healthy amount of glass panes to apply to said walls and rooves. You can put planters, trellises, bonsai pots, you name it, inside the protected area (everything inside but the roof) and it will grow without supervision, provided you have a spout or sprinkler system in place to keep everything hydrated. Placement conditions: the climate station's ice/water face needs to face in the direction the roof slopes up and down (hereby referred as x-axis) and the doors have all to be placed on the walls gfacing in the z-direction, so perpendicular to the former. Lastly, if the structure has an odd number of blocks along the x axis, the topmost line of roof blocks have to be hit with a tfc hammer to be flattened. Sprinklers and spouts only accept fresh water, so pump that up automatically.

tasks.longDescription: If this seems too expensive for you right now, come back once you have access to steel. Not only does it yield more, the pig iron also needs no forging to fit into place.

quests.name: Flaming Alloy
quests.description: The codex speaks of some alloy called dawnstone- a mix of copper and gold that's especially effective at channeling ember. The closest we've gotten was rose gold, something seems to be missing. Maybe try to "anneal" it using some very hot substance? The other elemental liquids are too volatile for it, but a melter could probably make some pyrotheum, albeit at a horrible exchange rate.

tasks.longDescription: You'll need a mixer centrifuge, at least one melter, and a stamper to re-solidify the finished dawnstone.

quests.name: Mechanical Pumps
quests.description: If you need to pick up liquids in the world, here's a few devices that make that possible. Keep in mind that it is possible to use MysticalMechanics Axles to power the mechanical pump, but it has to be run through a transmission box first.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you have made the following items:

quests.name: Ceramic Guardians
quests.description: These bricked constructs must be protecting the structures from intruders. At some point that might have been the assortment of monsters down there, but over time they must've undergone some change through natural selection. With noone around to repair them, those who kept attacking the mobs were bound to be taken out eventually. You with your completely alien appearance have to have sparked their interest once more. They hit hard, and if they can't reach you, they shoot fiery projectiles, probably originating from the same geothermal energy that keeps them going. These projectiles cannot be blocked using a shield, so be extra careful around future ones. Side note: they can drop an eye of the ancients when killed with a pickaxe.

tasks.longDescription: You have killed the following creature: I'm going to show this fight to the rest of the crew, we haven't had a proper sports event to watch in weeks!

quests.name: Steam Pressure
quests.description: Thanks to the design of the combustion engine inside the liquid compressor, you should be able to use steam to fuel it, and quite efficiently at that.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you have obtained this item:

quests.name: Compressors
quests.description: To actually generate any pressure, we'll need a compressor of some kind. the most basic one is a stirling engine type mechanism with some valves attached, basically compressing air using solid fuels. Beware that your setup can easily rupture if the pressure builds up too high. Best you make a few safety tube moldues and apply a redstone signal to get them down to a 5 bar threshhold.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you have obtained the following items:

quests.name: Infused Fuel
quests.description: Infused Ignatius... you don't say. I think you might've stumbled upon something that'll finally let us melt down that pesky tungsten. and half of your outpost too, while we're at it, so be cautious when handling it.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you have obtained this item. Don't hold it too close to the tablet's scanner though. these things are more expensive than they look.

quests.name: Tar Cracking
quests.description: With our newly acquired, and overly abundant, steam, you could try and mix it with some of that tar from those surface pools. Together with the added heat from a mixer centrifuge, it should be enough to crack it into usable oil.

tasks.longDescription: Get a hold of this item:

quests.name: Smeltery, at last
quests.description: With this Tungsten, we finally have a material to hold seared bricks together in a way that won't melt while still giving it room to expand so it doesn't crack under all the thermal stress. This should allow us to cast things like large plates aswell as make some interesting new alloys.

quests.name: Mining Drill
quests.description: One of the new items you have access to with the exchange pedestal is the Blasting Core, aka a Makeshift combustion engine. Using this, you can make a proper mining Drill! melt down some Alumentum for some early fuel, or use diesel if you have access to oil already. Later on, you can also get to upgrading the drill with better heads and additional components.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you've made the following item:

quests.name: Pressure Chamber
quests.description: The pressure chamber is a rather pricy structure comprised of two or more floodgates for items and a valve fitted into the faces of a 3x3x3 to 5x5x5 structure of compressed iron. To function as an extraction device, we will also need a vacuum pump to turn positive pressure from the compressor into negative pressure for the chamber. Other processes like making more compressed iron will use positive pressure though, so keep that in mind and make a second chamber if needed.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you have gotten your hands on a full setup for a vacuumized pressure chamber. Please note that you will have to stand on the inside if you want to place the hatch for the output.

quests.name: Tungsten
quests.description: With Adequate Fuel at hand, we are now able to melt tungsten out of its ore, wolframite. Make sure to use a bellows and tuyere for this one. You'll be getting about 2-7 ingots worth, which isn't much for all the time that the ore takes to heat up. To get more bang for your buck, consider making tungstensteel instead! it's up to 50 times cheaper, but harder to work due to its even higher melting point.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you have obtained the following item:

quests.name: Mechanical Power
quests.description: Now that we have access to steam, it's time to put it to use. As of now, ember is still kind of costly due to the lava involved in its refinement, so using it for such menial tasks as operating a stamper seems very inefficient, especially if the device is already kinetic in nature. With this simple steam engine, you'll be able to use steam and some other combustible liquids to make rotary power. Be warned though, it will happily guzzle away your steam reserves if you don't restrict its input, so only allow it liquid when it's actually doing something useful.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you have made the following item:

quests.name: Steam Power
quests.description: Ember-related machines can get very hot, but in a very controlled manner. we can use this to boil water into steam using a small and simple vessel. Just attach it to an ember producer or -consumer and feed it water from the sides. Do note that the boiler may explode if the steam isn't extracted, which you do from the top. this won't happen on its own, so make sure to use a pump of some sort.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you've made this item:

quests.name: Blast Furnace
quests.description: Using some of the archaic bricks from the golems along with some metal scrap and fire clay, you should be able to construct a blast furnace. To make it, place down a crucible with the furnace controller on top. then, build a chimney of fire bricks one block above the controller, with one brick block in every cardinal direction. To complete it, place 12 wrought iron (or any other Tier 3+ Tool Metal) sheets on the outer sides of the fire bricks, covering them completely. This chimney layout can be stacked up to 5 times, with each layer holding 4 more fuel and ore. Lastly, put in the tuyere and make sure that the bellows is facing the controller. If you're confused by these instructions, consider consulting Collins' Guide.

tasks.longDescription: Please show me that you have obtained the following items: I'll go with wrought iron here for the sheets simply because it's the most abundant, but aluminium, boron, and later steel itself can be used.

quests.name: Coke Oven Battery
quests.description: While coke ovens are nice and efficient, they are obnoxiously slow. Introducing: the coke oven battery! This thing, despite making use of steel and engineering blocks, is entirely obtainable with only steam-age tech and can be expanded about indefinitely, though a minimum size one can usually sustain a base of your tech level all on its own. While it may initially look slow, this thing processes 8 items at once, per slot. Beware though that it will not stop if either output is full. Excess creosote is voided and excess coke/charcoal is dropped on the ground. Better make an overflow shutoff with a buffer if you're gonna put its full capacity to use.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you have made the required blocks for a minimum size coke battery:

quests.name: The hunt for oil
quests.description: If cracking tar or waiting for better technology for a pumpjack isn't to your liking, you can always try locating actual crude oil yourself using this simple tool. be warned, however: the yield is meager at best, and the deposits tend to be quite far down.

tasks.longDescription: Show me this item to update your mission progress.

quests.name: Mechanical Centrifuge
quests.description: One way to extract things is to spin them really fast. When powered with mechanical energy, like through one of Zenon's essentia motors, this Machine does just that. Just do me a favor and mind the speed settings.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you have acquired these items:

quests.name: Pressurized
quests.description: By subjecting iron to some intense pressures, you can create this weird metal i've dubbed compressed iron. as its name implies, it is exceptionally resilient to pressure and could come in handy for our operation here. Unfortunately, this resilience is also the reason you can't hammer it into plates or rods, so you'll have to use the ingots like they are.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you have made the following item:

quests.name: Plastic
quests.description: Using some LPG and coal in a thermopneumatic plant yields a good amountof plastic. It's not quite HDPE-grade, but it should do for any applications you may have for it.

quests.name: Harnessing the Core
quests.description: So i was right! About being wrong, that is. This thermal cell does seem to store some kind of Energy that I should probably talk to Zenon about. To refuel them, you will need an active core extractor. "Active" in this case means two things: 1) The extractor pipe going down is lit up with orange dots. 2) the transfer unit's plate has been removed and the switch put into the middle position. The mechanism's a bit rusted, so using your trusty claw and hammer might be of need.

tasks.longDescription: Show me one fully charged thermal cell. Now the obvious question: we have the energy in this cell. How do we get it out?

quests.name: Thermite
quests.description: Made from aluminium and some iron oxide, this aluminothermic substance can melt even titanium with no bellows required. Sprinkle in some extra carbon, and you can even use it to make steel without having to worry about tuyere durability. you will have to get a stable supply of aluminium though.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you have obtained the following item:

quests.name: Ancient Knowledge
quests.description: I found that the core of one of those golems contains information on these structures in their programming. Since it's all logic-based, you should have no trouble deciphering it. Encase it in a few additional bricks for style, and you should be able to make your very own guide book on this stuff.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you've made this item:

quests.name: Simple Item Logistics
quests.description: Truly smart item transfer might not be obtainable at your tech level, but these "clotheslines" at least won't over-extract like the leather conveyors do. To connect 2 anchors, hold right-click on the first one and move your crosshair to the second one before letting go. Power them mechanically through an axle on the bottom. Anchors can be attached to any side of a block and will attempt to insert items to the side they're connected to.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you have made the following items:

quests.name: Alchemy 2, electric boogaloo
quests.description: Dawnstone has some astounding properties. One of them is that using a pattern of ash, and a burst of ember, you can use it to fuse items into new and interesting forms! I'm almost  certain that this will come in handy. To use it, place the items on the exchange pedestal in the required shape and kickstart the process with a beam cannon directed at the tablet. the cannon requires ember and a redstone pulse. Unlike other recipes, these have to be figured out through trial and error.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you've made the following items:

quests.name: Auto-Smithing
quests.description: Dawnstone's amazing properties allow metals around it to become much more malleable. this means that if you hit anything placed on this special anvil often enough (or hard enough) you can essentially forge it like on an anvil. What's more, it can also weld things if you place two items on the anvil. Lastly, you can automate it using a mechanical hammer. Finished items will be either spat out into the world or deposited in a bin below. If it produced multiple different outputs, only one type can be stored in the bin.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you've made the following items:

quests.name: Long Distance Transport
quests.description: I've overheard Hanai and Lerida talk about how thinly spread the ores are on this planet. I'd bet that that would also mean that you'll need some way to connect small mining facilities with your main base. Since dimensional transceivers are still a 'bit' out of reach, i'd suggest you use steam technology's signature vehicle: the train! well, minecart. Close enough.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you've obtained the following items:

quests.name: Materials of the Deep
quests.description: These Ruins seem to be made of a remarkable material. it is completely impervious to any breaking that doesn't press against the entirety of its surface. In other words, your pickaxe won't do a thing, but explosives will. Though beware the resulting cave-ins if you decide to take these blocks home with you. Also, it would be wise to get yourself one of Dr. Mickelus' Hammers of at least tier 3 plus a tool with a claw so you can try to break open some of the more valuable-looking things.

tasks.longDescription: I'd like you to send me some samples of this stuff, to see what other properties it has. most notably, these core extractors. They are the obvious centerpiece of this whole structure, so i'd like one of these up here so i can examine how they work. Once again, you can use explosives to dismantle them safely.

quests.name: Fluid Extraction
quests.description: Not every source of liquids is eager to share it with your pipes. Here are a few devices to extract fluids that are available at your tech level. Note that the IE pump doesn't require Power when extracting from a tank, only when pumping fluids in the world.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you've made the following items:

quests.name: THE POWER WITHIN!
quests.description: These crystals eminate an astounding amount of heat. I've sent a sample to Zenon, and we've come to the conclusion that it's definitely no normal exothermic reaction, nor does it seem to be nuclear in nature. It's definitely connected to the planet's strange energies. That codex you built shows that we can set those energies free by burning them in a copper and iron vessel, a pressure refinery. It will need to be fed ember shards and lava into the bottom section. the activated heat can then be extracted at the top.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you have obtained the Refinery aswell as a bit of Infrastructure to transfer the Ember,
